classification.difficultyReason: Compare squared side lengths, including decimal lengths, and identify the angle opposite the longest side.

content.prompt: Decide whether each of the triangles below is right-angled. If it is, name the right angle.

spec.description: Triangle ABC with A upper right, B lower left and C lower right; no right-angle mark. Source blue outlines are rendered in house black.
spec.answerVisibility: All supplied lengths and vertex labels visible; no answer marks.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}14^2+16^2&=196+256\\14^2+16^2&=452\\20^2&=400\end{align*}$$
Since $14^2+16^2\ne20^2$, the triangle is not right-angled.

spec.description: Triangle with AB vertical, BC horizontal and AC diagonal; no right-angle mark. Source blue outlines are rendered in house black.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}12^2+16^2&=144+256\\12^2+16^2&=400\\20^2&=400\end{align*}$$
Since $12^2+16^2=20^2$, the triangle is right-angled by the converse of Pythagoras’ theorem. The right angle is $\angle ABC$, opposite $AC$.

spec.description: Oblique triangle with A upper left, B right and C below; no right-angle mark. Source blue outlines are rendered in house black.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}6^2+2.5^2&=36+6.25\\6^2+2.5^2&=42.25\\6.5^2&=42.25\end{align*}$$
Since $6^2+2.5^2=6.5^2$, the triangle is right-angled by the converse of Pythagoras’ theorem. The right angle is $\angle ACB$, opposite $AB$.

spec.description: Triangle with A lower left, B above and C right; no right-angle mark. Source blue outlines are rendered in house black.

answer.worked:
